learn.b: The Song dynasty ran its empire with a civil service exam based on Confucian learning. Neo-Confucianism mixed Confucian ideas with Buddhism and Daoism. Fast-growing Champa rice from Vietnam fed a booming population, and the Grand Canal moved goods north and south.

The Abbasid Caliphate weakened, and new Turkic Muslim states took power: the Seljuks, the Mamluks in Egypt, and the Delhi Sultanate in India. Muslim scholars kept and built on Greek learning in math, medicine and astronomy.

Hindu Vijayanagara rivaled the Delhi Sultanate. The Bhakti movement taught personal devotion to one god. Srivijaya grew rich by controlling the Strait of Malacca, while the Khmer Empire built Angkor Wat.

The Mexica ruled from Tenochtitlan using tribute and chinampa farms. The Inca used the mit'a labor system and quipu records. In Africa, Mali grew rich from gold, and Great Zimbabwe traded across the Indian Ocean. Europe was decentralized under feudalism and the Catholic Church.

qs.q: Which innovation helped Song China's population grow so quickly?
qs.why: Champa rice ripened fast and resisted drought, so farmers could grow two crops a year.

qs.q: The Inca made people work on state projects for a set time. This system was called…
qs.why: The mit'a was a labor tax: communities sent workers to build roads, terraces and forts.

qs.q: Srivijaya's power came mainly from controlling the Strait of Malacca.
qs.why: Srivijaya taxed ships passing through the strait between the Indian Ocean and South China Sea.

qs.q: Match each state to its city or monument
Neo-Confucianism blended Confucian ideas with…
qs.why: Song thinkers added Buddhist and Daoist ideas about the self and the universe to Confucian ethics.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
The Delhi Sultanate was ruled by Hindu kings.
qs.why: It was a Muslim sultanate ruling over a mostly Hindu population.

qs.q: The Bhakti movement emphasized…
o: Personal devotion to a single god
qs.why: Bhakti taught emotional devotion to one deity and often challenged caste barriers.

learn.b: Overland routes carried luxury goods like silk and porcelain. Caravanserai (roadside inns) sheltered merchants. Banking tools such as bills of exchange and Chinese flying cash made long-distance trade easier.

The Mongols built the largest land empire in history. Their Pax Mongolica made the Silk Roads safer, which spread trade, ideas and also the bubonic plague. The empire split into khanates such as the Yuan in China and the Ilkhanate in Persia.

Monsoon winds made sailing predictable. Ships like dhows and junks, and tools like the compass and astrolabe, carried goods between East Africa, India and China. Swahili city-states mixed Bantu and Arab culture. Zheng He led huge Ming treasure fleets.
Camels and camel saddles made the Sahara crossable. West African gold was traded for Saharan salt, making Mali very rich. Travelers like Ibn Battuta and Marco Polo recorded these networks.

qs.q: What made Indian Ocean trade predictable?
qs.why: Monsoon winds change direction by season, so sailors could plan round trips.

qs.q: The main exchange in trans-Saharan trade was…
o: West African gold for Saharan salt
qs.why: Gold from West Africa moved north; salt from the Sahara moved south.

qs.q: The Pax Mongolica made Silk Road travel safer, which also helped spread the Black Death.
qs.why: More trade and travel across Mongol lands carried plague from Central Asia to the Mediterranean.

qs.q: Match each traveler to what they are known for
pairs: Hajj with huge amounts of gold

qs.q: Swahili city-states like Kilwa blended…
qs.why: Swahili is a Bantu language with many Arabic words, reflecting this mix.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
A caravanserai was…
o: A roadside inn for merchants and their animals
qs.why: Caravanserai let traders rest safely along the Silk Roads and helped spread ideas too.

learn.b: The Ottoman, Safavid and Mughal empires used cannons and guns to expand. Mehmed II took Constantinople in 1453. The Ottomans used the devshirme, taking Christian boys to train as janissary soldiers and officials.

The Ottomans were Sunni and the Safavids were Shia, which fueled their wars. Mughal emperor Akbar practiced religious tolerance and ended the jizya tax on non-Muslims. In Europe, Luther's 1517 protest started the Protestant Reformation.
The Manchu founded the Qing dynasty in 1644 and made Han men wear the queue hairstyle. Tokugawa Japan limited contact with outsiders.
Rulers built monuments to show legitimacy, like the Taj Mahal (a tomb built by Shah Jahan) and Versailles. Sikhism emerged in India, mixing ideas from Hinduism and Islam.

qs.q: The Ottoman devshirme system…
o: Took Christian boys to train as soldiers and officials
Gave land to nobles for military service
Sent merchants to trade with Europe
qs.why: Boys were converted and trained to serve the sultan, including as janissaries.

qs.q: Match each empire to its feature
The Ottoman–Safavid rivalry was partly driven by the Sunni–Shia split.
qs.why: The Sunni Ottomans and Shia Safavids fought repeatedly over land and religion.

qs.q: Akbar strengthened Mughal rule over a Hindu majority by…
o: Promoting religious tolerance and ending the jizya
qs.why: Tolerance won support from Hindu elites and helped hold the empire together.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
Sikhism combines elements of…
qs.why: Guru Nanak drew on Hindu and Muslim ideas and taught devotion to one God.

qs.q: Akbar built the Taj Mahal as a mosque.
qs.why: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

learn.b: The caravel, lateen sail, compass and astrolabe let Europeans sail farther. Portugal's Prince Henry sponsored exploration. Columbus reached the Caribbean in 1492 and Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498.
Plants, animals and diseases crossed the Atlantic. Smallpox killed huge numbers of Native Americans. Potatoes and maize fed Afro-Eurasia, while horses, cattle and sugarcane came to the Americas.
Sugar plantations drove the Atlantic slave trade and the Middle Passage. Spain used the encomienda and later the hacienda, and built a casta system ranking people by race and birthplace.

Joint-stock companies like the Dutch East India Company shared risk among investors. Mercantilism pushed states to gain wealth through colonies. Silver from Potosí flowed to China. Resistance included the Pueblo Revolt (1680) and maroon communities.

qs.q: Which item traveled from the Americas to Afro-Eurasia in the Columbian Exchange?
qs.why: Potatoes came from the Andes and helped populations grow in Europe and Asia. The others went the other way.

qs.q: Mercantilism is the idea that a state grows rich by…
o: Exporting more than it imports and using colonies
Letting markets run with no government control
qs.why: Mercantilist states wanted a favorable balance of trade and raw materials from colonies.

qs.q: Match each explorer to the achievement
Spanish silver from the Americas flowed into China, partly through the Manila galleons.
qs.why: Ming China demanded silver for taxes, so American silver crossed the Pacific via Manila.

qs.q: The casta system in Spanish America ranked people by…
qs.why: Peninsulares were at the top, then creoles, mestizos, and enslaved and Indigenous people below.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
A joint-stock company…
o: Let many investors share risk and profit
Was owned only by the king
Was a type of colonial tax
qs.why: Selling shares spread risk, which made costly voyages possible.

learn.b: Thinkers used reason to question kings and churches. Locke argued for natural rights, Montesquieu for separation of powers, Rousseau for the social contract, and Voltaire for freedom of religion and speech.

The American Revolution (1776), French Revolution (1789) and Haitian Revolution (1791) spread these ideas. Toussaint Louverture led Haiti, the only successful large slave revolt to create a state. Creole leaders like Simón Bolívar freed much of South America.
People began to see themselves as nations with shared language and history. Italy unified in 1861 and Germany in 1871.

Industry began in Britain thanks to coal, iron, rivers, colonies and capital. Watt's steam engine and the factory system changed work. A second industrial revolution brought steel, electricity and chemicals.

qs.q: Why did industrialization start in Britain?
o: Coal and iron deposits, rivers, and capital from colonies
A large enslaved workforce in factories
Lack of competition from other countries
qs.why: Britain had the natural resources, money and markets that factories needed.

qs.q: Match each thinker to the idea
The Haitian Revolution created an independent state through a slave revolt.
qs.why: Haiti declared independence in 1804 after enslaved people defeated French forces.

qs.q: Simón Bolívar led independence movements in…
qs.why: Bolívar helped free Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
The Second Industrial Revolution was built on…
qs.why: After 1850, new industries in steel, electricity and chemicals took off.

qs.q: Creoles in Latin America were…
o: People of European descent born in the Americas
qs.why: Creoles resented peninsulares, who held the top jobs, and led many independence movements.

learn.b: Industrial nations wanted raw materials and markets. Social Darwinism was used to justify conquest. At the Berlin Conference (1884–85), Europeans divided Africa among themselves.

Britain beat Qing China in the Opium Wars, starting in 1839, and took Hong Kong. India saw the Sepoy Rebellion in 1857, after which the British crown ruled directly. China also faced the Taiping and Boxer rebellions.
Japan's Meiji Restoration (1868) rapidly modernized the country with state-led industry. China's Self-Strengthening Movement had less success.
After slavery ended, indentured servants from India and China worked on plantations worldwide. Workers formed unions, and Marx and Engels wrote the Communist Manifesto in 1848.

qs.q: The Berlin Conference was held to…
o: Divide Africa among European powers without war
qs.why: European powers set rules for claiming African land, with no Africans present.

qs.q: Japan's Meiji Restoration is known for…
qs.why: The Meiji government copied Western technology and built railways, factories and a modern army.

qs.q: Match each event to its description
After slavery was abolished, many indentured servants from India and China worked on plantations abroad.
qs.why: They signed contracts to work for years, often in harsh conditions, in places like the Caribbean.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
Social Darwinism was used to…
qs.why: It misused ideas about survival of the fittest to claim some peoples should rule others.

learn.b: Causes are often remembered as MAIN: militarism, alliances, imperialism and nationalism. It was a total war, using whole economies and colonial troops. The Treaty of Versailles (1919) blamed Germany and demanded reparations.
The Mexican Revolution began in 1910. In 1917, Lenin's Bolsheviks took power in Russia and later formed the USSR.

The Great Depression began in 1929. Some states expanded government spending, following Keynes. Others turned to fascism, like Mussolini's Italy and Hitler's Germany. Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931 for resources.
WWII (1939–1945) was even deadlier. It included the Holocaust and ended in the Pacific after atomic bombs were dropped on Japan.

qs.q: The causes of World War I are often summed up as MAIN. What does it stand for?
qs.why: These four long-term causes built tension before the 1914 assassination sparked war.

qs.q: The Treaty of Versailles…
qs.why: The war guilt clause and reparations caused anger that later helped the Nazis.

qs.q: Total war means a country mobilizes its whole economy and population for the war effort.
qs.why: Factories, women workers, rationing and propaganda all served the war.

qs.q: Match each leader to the movement
Put these events in order, earliest first
Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931 mainly to…
qs.why: Japan had few natural resources and wanted Manchuria's coal and iron.

learn.b: The U.S. and USSR competed after 1945. The U.S. used containment to stop communism, with the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan aid. NATO and the Warsaw Pact were rival alliances. Proxy wars were fought in Korea and Vietnam.
The Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962 nearly caused nuclear war. Gorbachev's reforms, glasnost and perestroika, came before the USSR collapsed in 1991.
Mao's communists won in 1949. The Great Leap Forward caused a terrible famine.

India won independence in 1947 through Gandhi's nonviolent movement, but partition caused mass violence. Ghana, led by Nkrumah, won independence peacefully in 1957, while Algeria fought a violent war against France. Many new states joined the Non-Aligned Movement.

qs.q: The U.S. Cold War policy of containment aimed to…
qs.why: Containment guided aid, alliances and wars from Europe to Asia.

qs.q: The Non-Aligned Movement was made up of countries that…
o: Refused to side with either superpower
qs.why: Leaders like Nehru wanted to avoid being pulled into the Cold War.

qs.q: Algeria won independence from France through a mostly peaceful process.
qs.why: Algeria fought a long, violent war of independence from 1954 to 1962.

qs.q: Match each leader to the event
Put these events in order, earliest first
The Marshall Plan was…
o: U.S. economic aid to rebuild Western Europe
qs.why: Aid helped Europe recover and made communism less attractive there.

learn.b: The Green Revolution used high-yield seeds and fertilizers to grow more food. Medicine wiped out smallpox, but diseases like HIV/AIDS spread. The internet and cell phones connected the world.

Many states moved toward free markets. Deng Xiaoping opened China to markets from 1978. Trade deals like NAFTA and groups like the WTO and EU lowered trade barriers. Multinational corporations grew powerful.
The United Nations was founded in 1945 to promote peace and cooperation. Human rights movements worked for women's rights and the end of apartheid in South Africa.
Critics say globalization widens wealth gaps and exploits cheap labor. Burning fossil fuels has driven climate change.

qs.q: The Green Revolution increased food production through…
qs.why: It fed growing populations in places like India and Mexico, but used lots of water and chemicals.

qs.q: Deng Xiaoping's reforms in China…
o: Opened the economy to market forces
qs.why: China kept one-party rule but allowed private business and foreign investment.

qs.q: The United Nations was founded after World War II to promote international cooperation.
qs.why: It was created in 1945 to replace the failed League of Nations.

qs.q: Match each organization to its purpose
pairs: Economic and political union in Europe

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
items: Mandela elected president of South Africa

qs.q: A common criticism of globalization is that it…
o: Widens wealth gaps and exploits cheap labor
qs.why: Critics point to sweatshops and gaps between rich and poor countries.

learn.b: Between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, Sumerian city-states built ziggurat temples and invented cuneiform writing. Later, Hammurabi of Babylon published one of the first written law codes.
Yearly Nile floods made farming reliable. Pharaohs ruled as god-kings, built pyramids as tombs, and scribes wrote in hieroglyphs.
Cities like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had grid streets and drainage systems. Their script has never been fully deciphered.
The Shang carved questions to ancestors on oracle bones. The Zhou claimed the Mandate of Heaven: heaven grants the right to rule and takes it away from unjust rulers.

qs.q: Hammurabi's Code was…
o: A written law code from Babylon
qs.why: It listed laws and punishments publicly, like "an eye for an eye".

qs.q: The Indus Valley script has been fully deciphered.
qs.why: Scholars still cannot read it, so much about Indus society is unknown.

qs.q: Match each civilization to its writing or site
The Mandate of Heaven said that…
o: Heaven gives a ruler power and can take it away if he is unjust
Power passes to the oldest daughter
qs.why: The Zhou used it to justify overthrowing the Shang, and later dynasties used it too.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first

learn.b: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian Empire. Persia ruled through satraps (provincial governors), built the Royal Road, and generally tolerated local religions.

Athens developed direct democracy. Alexander the Great spread Greek (Hellenistic) culture to Egypt and India. Rome went from republic to empire under Augustus and built roads, aqueducts and a lasting legal system.
The Han dynasty expanded trade along the Silk Roads, used Confucian officials, and invented paper.
Ashoka of the Maurya Empire turned to Buddhism after the bloody battle of Kalinga and spread it widely. The Gupta Empire had a golden age in math, including the concept of zero.

qs.q: Ashoka is best known for…
o: Spreading Buddhism after the Kalinga war
qs.why: Horrified by the violence at Kalinga, he promoted Buddhist ideas across his empire.

qs.q: The Han dynasty is credited with inventing paper.
qs.why: Paper made record-keeping and learning much easier.

qs.q: Match each ruler to the achievement
Persian satraps were…
qs.why: Satraps ran provinces for the king, who checked on them with spies.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
items: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

qs.q: A key achievement of the Gupta golden age was…
o: The concept of zero and decimal numbers
qs.why: Gupta mathematicians developed zero and place value, later spread by Arab scholars.

apq.stim: A 14th-century traveler described the king of Mali wearing gold ornaments, while scholars studied in the mosques of Timbuktu.
apq.src: Paraphrased from Ibn Battuta's travel account, 1350s
apq.q: The wealth described most directly resulted from…
o: Trans-Saharan trade in gold and salt
apq.why: Mali controlled gold fields and the trade routes across the Sahara.

apq.stim: Chart: silver exports from Spanish America rose sharply between 1550 and 1650, with a large share ending up in China.
apq.q: Which factor best explains China's demand for silver in this period?
o: The Ming required taxes to be paid in silver
The Qing banned paper money in 1400
Europeans forced China to buy silver
apq.why: The Ming "single whip" tax reform made silver the basis of payments.

apq.stim: In 1839, Qing official Lin Zexu wrote to Queen Victoria asking how Britain could sell opium in China while banning it at home.
o: Qing efforts to stop the opium trade and loss of silver
British plans to colonize all of China
apq.why: Opium imports reversed the flow of silver and caused addiction, leading to the Opium Wars.

apq.stim: In 1872, the Japanese government opened the Tomioka silk mill using French machines and advisers.
apq.q: This development is best understood as an example of…
apq.why: The Meiji state funded model factories to catch up with the West.

apq.stim: "Men are born and remain free and equal in rights."
apq.src: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, 1789, Article 1
apq.q: The ideas in this document most directly inspired…
apq.why: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue applied the same ideas of liberty and equality to themselves.

apq.stim: In 1955, leaders of 29 Asian and African countries met at Bandung, Indonesia, to discuss cooperation and opposition to colonialism.
apq.q: The Bandung Conference is most closely connected to…
apq.why: Bandung laid the groundwork for nations that refused to join either Cold War bloc.

apq.stim: At the Mughal court, Akbar hosted debates among Muslims, Hindus, Jains, Zoroastrians and Christians.
apq.src: Historical summary of Mughal court records
apq.q: Akbar's policy was most likely meant to…
o: Win the loyalty of a religiously diverse population
apq.why: Tolerance helped a Muslim ruler govern a Hindu-majority empire.

apq.stim: Ship records from the 1700s show millions of enslaved Africans carried to Brazil and the Caribbean.
apq.src: Data summary, Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database
apq.q: The main reason for this demand was…
apq.why: Sugar plantations were brutal and needed huge numbers of workers.

apq.stim: Graph: global carbon dioxide emissions stayed low before 1850, then rose steeply, especially after 1950.
apq.q: This trend is most directly connected to…
o: The fall of the Mongol Empire
apq.why: Burning coal, oil and gas for industry and transport released the carbon.

apq.stim: In 1930, Gandhi led thousands on a march to the sea to make salt, breaking a British law.
apq.q: The Salt March is an example of…
apq.why: Gandhi used peaceful lawbreaking to show the injustice of British rule.

apq.stim: Article 231 of the 1919 treaty made Germany accept responsibility for the war and its damage.
apq.q: Resentment of this treaty most directly contributed to…
o: The rise of the Nazi Party
apq.why: Hitler promised to undo the treaty, which won him support.

apq.stim: Ibn Battuta worked as a judge (qadi) in places as far apart as Delhi and the Maldives.
apq.q: He could do this mainly because…
o: Shared Islamic law and Arabic linked Dar al-Islam
The Mongols ruled all of these lands
Europeans hired him as an ambassador
apq.why: Islam created a common legal and cultural world across many states.

learn.b: Before 1492, Native peoples adapted to their environments. Maize farming in the Southwest supported settled Pueblo societies with irrigation. Plains peoples were often mobile, and Northeast groups mixed farming and hunting.
Spain used the encomienda system to force Native people to work. Las Casas argued against this cruelty in the Valladolid debate against Sepúlveda. The Columbian Exchange brought horses and disease.
France built fur-trade alliances with Native peoples. The Dutch focused on trade from New Amsterdam. England later sent large numbers of settlers to farm.

qs.q: The spread of maize in the Southwest led to…
qs.why: Reliable maize harvests let Pueblo peoples build permanent towns.

qs.q: Bartolomé de las Casas argued against the harsh treatment of Native peoples.
qs.why: He wrote about Spanish cruelty and pushed for reform.

qs.q: Match each colonizer to its approach
Put these events in order, earliest first
The encomienda system gave Spanish colonists…
o: The right to Native labor and tribute
qs.why: Colonists were supposed to protect and Christianize workers, but it was abusive in practice.

learn.b: Jamestown survived by growing tobacco for export. The House of Burgesses (1619) was an early elected assembly. Bacon's Rebellion (1676) pushed planters toward enslaved African labor instead of indentured servants.
Puritans built towns around churches and families. The Mayflower Compact was an early self-government agreement.
Britain followed salutary neglect, loosely enforcing trade laws. The Great Awakening religious revival challenged established churches.

qs.q: One result of Bacon's Rebellion was that Virginia planters…
qs.why: Planters feared armed poor white servants and turned to slavery instead.

qs.q: The Great Awakening was a religious revival that challenged established churches.
qs.why: Preachers like Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield stressed personal faith.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Worked for years to pay for passage

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first

learn.b: The French and Indian War ended in 1763 and left Britain in debt. The Proclamation of 1763 and taxes like the Stamp Act (1765) angered colonists, who protested taxation without representation.
The Declaration of Independence (1776), written mainly by Jefferson, used Enlightenment ideas. Washington led the Continental Army.
The Articles of Confederation were weak, as Shays' Rebellion (1786) showed. The Constitution (1787) created a stronger federal government. Anti-Federalists demanded a Bill of Rights.

qs.q: Shays' Rebellion showed that…
o: The Articles of Confederation were too weak
qs.why: The national government could not raise an army to stop the uprising.

qs.q: Anti-Federalists demanded a Bill of Rights before supporting the Constitution.
qs.why: They feared a strong central government would threaten individual liberties.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
Match each founder to their role

learn.b: Jefferson bought the Louisiana Territory from France in 1803, doubling the country. In Marbury v. Madison (1803), the Supreme Court claimed judicial review. The Monroe Doctrine (1823) warned Europe not to colonize the Americas again.
Voting expanded to almost all white men. Andrew Jackson signed the Indian Removal Act (1830), which led to the Trail of Tears.

Canals like the Erie Canal, railroads and factories tied regions together. The Second Great Awakening inspired reforms such as abolition, temperance and the women's rights meeting at Seneca Falls (1848).

qs.q: Marbury v. Madison established…
qs.why: The Court gave itself the power to strike down laws that break the Constitution.

qs.q: The Monroe Doctrine warned European powers against new colonization in the Americas.
qs.why: It became a lasting principle of U.S. foreign policy.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Linked the Great Lakes to New York City
Forced relocation west of the Mississippi

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
Jacksonian democracy mainly…
o: Expanded voting to most white men
qs.why: Property requirements for voting were dropped in most states.

learn.b: Manifest Destiny drove westward expansion and the Mexican-American War (1846). New land reopened the fight over slavery: the Compromise of 1850, the Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854) and the Dred Scott decision (1857).
Lincoln's election in 1860 led Southern states to secede. The war lasted from 1861 to 1865. The Emancipation Proclamation (1863) freed enslaved people in Confederate states.
The 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments ended slavery, defined citizenship and protected voting regardless of race. Reconstruction ended in 1877 and Southern states rolled back many of these gains.

qs.q: The Dred Scott decision ruled that…
o: Black Americans were not citizens and Congress could not ban slavery in territories
Kansas must be a free state
qs.why: The ruling angered the North and pushed the country closer to war.

qs.q: Match each item to what it did
pairs: Freed enslaved people in Confederate states

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
The Kansas-Nebraska Act let settlers vote on whether to allow slavery.
qs.why: This popular sovereignty led to violence known as Bleeding Kansas.

qs.q: Manifest Destiny was the belief that…
o: The U.S. was meant to expand across the continent
The U.S. should stay out of foreign affairs
qs.why: It justified taking land from Mexico and Native nations.

learn.b: The transcontinental railroad was finished in 1869. Carnegie used vertical integration in steel, and Rockefeller used horizontal integration with Standard Oil.
Workers formed unions like the Knights of Labor and the AFL. Strikes and the Haymarket affair (1886) turned violent. Farmers formed the Populist Party to fight railroads and banks.
The Dawes Act (1887) broke up tribal lands into individual plots. Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) allowed "separate but equal" segregation. Millions of new immigrants came from southern and eastern Europe.

qs.q: Match each name to its role
Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) ruled that…
qs.why: It was overturned by Brown v. Board of Education in 1954.

qs.q: The Dawes Act broke up tribal land into individual plots.
qs.why: The goal was assimilation, and Native nations lost most of their land.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
Vertical integration means…
o: Controlling every step of production, from raw materials to sales
Buying out all competitors in one industry
qs.why: Carnegie owned the mines, ships and railroads that fed his steel mills.

learn.b: Muckraker journalists exposed corruption and bad working conditions. Reformers won new amendments, including the 19th Amendment (1920), which gave women the vote.
The U.S. entered WWI in 1917. Wilson proposed the Fourteen Points and the League of Nations, but the Senate rejected the treaty. The 1920s brought booming consumer culture.

The 1929 stock market crash began the Great Depression. FDR's New Deal used government programs for relief and reform. After Pearl Harbor (1941), the U.S. entered WWII, and Japanese Americans were forced into internment camps.

qs.q: The New Deal was…
o: FDR's programs for relief, recovery and reform
qs.why: Programs like Social Security still exist today.

qs.q: The 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote in 1920.
qs.why: Suffragists had campaigned for over 70 years since Seneca Falls.

qs.q: Match each person or group to what they did
Put these events in order, earliest first
During WWII, Executive Order 9066 led to…
qs.why: About 120,000 people of Japanese ancestry were forced into camps.

learn.b: The U.S. followed containment abroad. At home, McCarthyism accused people of being communists, often with little evidence.

Brown v. Board of Education (1954) ended legal school segregation. After Rosa Parks' arrest, the Montgomery bus boycott began. Leaders like Martin Luther King Jr. used nonviolence, leading to the Civil Rights Act (1964) and the Voting Rights Act (1965).
LBJ's Great Society fought poverty. The Vietnam War divided the country. Watergate led Nixon to resign in 1974.

qs.q: Brown v. Board of Education…
o: Overturned "separate but equal" in public schools
qs.why: The Court ruled that segregated schools were unequal by nature.

qs.q: Match each leader to the event
Put these events in order, earliest first
The Montgomery bus boycott began after Rosa Parks was arrested.
qs.why: The boycott lasted over a year and made King a national leader.

qs.q: McCarthyism refers to…
o: Accusing people of communism with little evidence
qs.why: Many lost jobs over accusations that were never proven.

learn.b: Ronald Reagan, elected in 1980, cut taxes and regulation and built up the military. The Cold War ended as the Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
NAFTA (1994) lowered trade barriers with Canada and Mexico. Computers and the internet changed work and daily life.
The September 11 attacks in 2001 led to the War on Terror. The 2008 financial crisis caused the Great Recession. Debates over immigration, health care and inequality continue.

qs.q: Reaganomics focused on…
qs.why: Supporters called it supply-side economics.

qs.q: NAFTA lowered trade barriers among the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
qs.why: It took effect in 1994 and was later replaced by the USMCA.

qs.q: Put these events in order, earliest first
Match each president to a key event
pairs: Tax cuts and Cold War buildup

apq.stim: Las Casas (1552) described Spanish colonists' cruelty toward Native peoples in the Caribbean.
apq.src: Paraphrased from A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies
apq.q: His account was most directly a response to…
apq.why: Encomienda forced labor caused massive suffering, which he condemned.

apq.stim: Virginia, 1676: Nathaniel Bacon led frontier settlers and servants who burned Jamestown.
o: A shift toward enslaved African labor
apq.why: Planters saw enslaved workers as easier to control than armed former servants.

apq.stim: Thomas Paine argued it was absurd for a small island to rule a whole continent.
o: Call for a monarchy in America
apq.why: Common Sense was a best-seller that pushed many toward independence.

apq.stim: In 1848, reformers at Seneca Falls modeled their Declaration of Sentiments on the Declaration of Independence, adding that all men and women are created equal.
apq.src: Paraphrased from the Declaration of Sentiments, 1848
o: The growth of reform movements tied to the Second Great Awakening
